must_fix.title: Focus trap leaks when the last focusable element is not rendered (display:none/hidden)
must_fix.evidence: focusableWithin in src/Dialog.tsx does not filter out unrendered elements, so trapTab treats a hidden button as `last` and does not preventDefault on Tab from the real last control. Dialog with <button>a</button><button style={{display:'none'}}>b</button>, then user.tab(): `start a` -> `after tab <body>...`. Focus leaves the modal. No test covers this.

report:
I found two Dialog bugs I'd want fixed before merging. Everything else checks out: `pnpm test` passes (86 tests in 4 files), `pnpm typecheck` passes, and the exports match the issue. The repo has no lint or format config and no changelog, so there was nothing else to run. Tabs (wrapping, skipping disabled tabs, Home/End, selection following focus, one tab stop, falling back from a disabled `defaultValue`) and Combobox (filtering, moving the active option with ArrowDown/ArrowUp and wrapping, Enter, Escape, "No results") behaved as the issue asks in my probes. **1. Focus doesn't go back to the opener when a dialog child uses `autoFocus`.** - **Cause:** `src/Dialog.tsx` records `document.activeElement` in a `useEffect` after the dialog has committed. React focuses an `autoFocus` child during the commit, so the element saved as "previous" is the input inside the dialog, not the opener. When the dialog closes, that input is unmounted and focus falls to ``. - **Why it matters:** the issue requires focus to return to whatever had it before opening, and `autoFocus` on the first field is common in dialogs. - **Repro:** I put a temporary test in the repo (deleted afterwards). It clicks an "Opener" button that sets `open`; the dialog contains ``; then it presses Escape. ``` in: after close:
``` The opener should have focus after closing, but `` does. **2. The focus trap leaks when the last focusable element is hidden.** - **Cause:** `focusableWithin` in `src/Dialog.tsx` only filters by selector and `tabIndex >= 0`. It doesn't exclude elements that aren't rendered (`display:none`, `hidden`). `trapTab` then treats an invisible element as "last". When Tab is pressed on the real last visible control, it doesn't call `preventDefault`, so focus leaves the dialog. - **Repro:** a dialog containing ``, then `user.tab()`: ``` start a after tab … ``` Focus went out of the dialog to `` instead of wrapping back to "a". No test covers hidden or unrendered focusables. **Nits** - `tests/index.test.ts` names its suite `"public exports (G1)"`. "G1" looks like a leftover label from a private plan. - ArrowDown on a combobox that already has a value makes the first option active rather than the selected one. The issue doesn't specify this, so it's a UX choice. - Tabs with every tab disabled have no tab stop, and there's no test for that case.
